title: TinyHttpd conformance of res.onAbort and res.relay over real sockets

metadata.Tags: 0.12.0, feasibility:high, request-a, tinyhttpd, adapter-conformance, relay, abort

acceptanceCriteria.text: Over a real TinyHttpd socket, when the client closes its connection while a `res.relay(in, -1)` or `res.stream(...)` transfer from a slow source is still copying, a listener registered with `res.onAbort` runs exactly once.
Over a real TinyHttpd socket, a listener registered on a response that completes normally is never run, also after the client closes the connection once the response was read.

Over a real TinyHttpd socket, a handler that sets no `Content-Type` and calls `res.relay(in, 5)` with a 5-byte stream gives the client a response with no `Content-Type` header, `Content-Length: 5` and the 5 body bytes.
Over a real TinyHttpd socket, `res.relay(in, -1)` gives a response without `Content-Length` whose complete body the client reads under the framing TinyHttpd chooses.

Over a real TinyHttpd socket, `res.relay(in, 5)` answers a `HEAD` request with `Content-Length: 5` and no body bytes, answers a `304` response with no body bytes and no `Content-Length` (TinyHttpd 3.1.1 never writes `Content-Length` on a 304, `ExchangeResponse.commit` at commit `e73cd5d`, which RFC 9110 §8.6 allows), and a `204` response with neither, and the next request on the same keep-alive connection is served normally.

Over a real TinyHttpd socket, `res.relay(in, 5)` with a stream that ends after 3 bytes closes the connection before 5 body bytes arrive, so the client sees a truncated response rather than a complete one.

traceLinks.notes: trace_intent=addition_site; abort notification and committed headers
built-in TinyHttpd exchange reports detected aborts

requirement: The system shall make the TinyHttpd adapter run `res.onAbort` listeners once when the client disconnects during a response and never after a normally completed one, and put `res.relay` responses on the wire with exactly the `Content-Type` the app set, the `Content-Length` taken from the length argument except on a `304`, where TinyHttpd 3.1.1 writes no `Content-Length` (PRD-271), the bodyless `HEAD`, `204` and `304` rules of FR-HTTP-037 and an aborted connection when the relayed stream ends early.
rationale:
AC-1 ← PRD-189; fills: PRD-189 / hole / for AC-1, AC-2, the in-memory adapter never reports an abort, so client-disconnect behaviour is tested over real TinyHttpd sockets (design D-069); AC-2 ← PRD-189; AC-3 ← PRD-190, PRD-38; fills: PRD-29 / hole / for AC-3, AC-4, AC-5, AC-6, the per-adapter wire behaviour of request A belongs to the adapter scopes (design D-004); AC-4 ← PRD-41, PRD-190; AC-5 ← PRD-190 (design D-031); AC-6 ← PRD-41, PRD-190.
- [2026-11-14] AC-5 ← PRD-271. TinyHttpd 3.1.1 writes no Content-Length on a 304 and is not changed by this target (PRD U-2), so the TinyHttpd criterion states that behaviour.
implementationNotes: - `TinyHttpdExchange` already registers and fires abort listeners through `AbortListeners` (`:267-283`) and adds committed headers verbatim (`:186-206`); check that TinyHttpd does not add its own `Content-Type` when none is set and keeps a `Content-Length` header on a `HEAD` response. TinyHttpd 3.1.1 drops the `Content-Length` of a `304` in `ExchangeResponse.commit` (commit `e73cd5d`), which AC-5 records as the expected TinyHttpd behaviour (PRD-271); do not work around it in the adapter. Socket tests follow the `RestApp.builder().httpAdapter(new TinyHttpdAdapter())...listen(0)` pattern with raw `Socket` clients.
